title: Executive leadership
decision: A quarterly report shows more sessions delivered. What would justify funding the next expansion?
practice: Select a resident outcome, hear from the people the count leaves out, and set a condition for continuing or revising the investment.
evidence: A reasoned funding choice and a date to check access.
authority: A formal budget commitment belongs with the authorized executive or governing body.

title: Managers and directors
decision: The callback dashboard improves after staff start closing cases at transfer. Do you extend the process to another unit?
practice: Compare completion at transfer with actual contact. Ask both teams and a community partner where people still wait.
evidence: A cross-unit decision naming who owns the callback and what would trigger a change.
authority: A manager can coordinate teams within their remit and take wider resource changes to the budget owner.

title: Supervisors
decision: The day shift sees an acting opportunity first. How do you choose coverage fairly with two days to prepare?
practice: Compare evidence of handoff skills from both shifts, communicate the criteria, and arrange coverage and feedback.
evidence: A defensible decision and a way for both shifts to hear about the next opening.
authority: Selection authority and applicable workplace processes must be checked for the actual assignment.

title: Policy and program professionals
decision: A proposed instruction resolves an internal delay but requires families to call a second office. What change do you recommend?
practice: Trace the handoff, invite a different account of the burden, and offer the policy owner two workable options.
evidence: A recommendation identifying the cost to residents and what can still be changed.
authority: The drafter recommends wording. The designated owner clears the change.

title: Licensing, investigations and program integrity
decision: Two units give different instructions. How do you establish what a person can rely on while the discrepancy is reviewed?
practice: Separate the reported facts from interpretation, find the authoritative instruction, and give the person a route for clarification.
evidence: An interim response and a named owner who can resolve the inconsistency.
authority: An analyst can surface the conflict. Only the appropriate authority makes the formal determination.

title: Eligibility and direct public service
decision: A person calls again after completing a referral. What can you do before sending them on to another office?
practice: Ask what the person understood and how they want to receive a response. Verify who will take the next step.
evidence: A handoff the person can describe, including how to ask for help if it stalls.
authority: Staff can clarify and connect within their assignment. Program determinations follow the authorized process.

title: Data, research and evaluation
decision: A monthly average improves while a partner reports longer waits. What does the evidence support saying?
practice: Check inclusion, missing cases and the definition of completion. Identify what else you would need before recommending expansion.
evidence: A finding with its limits and a follow-up question that could change the conclusion.
authority: Analysts establish what the data support. The service owner decides how to act.

title: Finance, contracts and grants
decision: Two proposals fit the funding limit. One is easier to administer and the other reaches people earlier in the service process. What belongs in your recommendation?
practice: Compare allowable uses, implementation burden, who benefits, and what you still need to know about costs.
evidence: A comparison that identifies who bears the cost of each option.
authority: A reviewer documents the trade-off. Approval follows the actual delegation of spending authority.

title: Enterprise professional services
decision: A new shared tool works for its designers. What would justify recommending it for staff who use different devices or access methods?
practice: Have users attempt the same task in different conditions. Bring the failures and possible fixes to the product owner.
evidence: A recommendation based on whether people can complete the task and recover from an error.
authority: The person advising on the tool can recommend and test. The owner authorizes a rollout.

title: Administrative and technical support
decision: An invitation asks for comment after the approval meeting. What can you change so the input can still influence the decision?
practice: Find the decision date and the owner. Propose a usable comment window and an accessible way to respond.
evidence: A revised invitation stating what is open, who will respond, and when.
authority: The coordinator can surface the timing problem. The decision owner confirms which choices remain open.
